doc.name: A — camping catalogue, stone plinth, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: three-season backpacking tent
Category: camping
Shot programme: stone plinth
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for a camping catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the macro detail insert in a stone plinth treatment.

SUBJECT. A three-season backpacking tent. The reference image governs silhouette, material finish and every printed mark. Reproduce the label text exactly as it appears; never invent new copy, logos or claims.

CAMERA. Extreme macro on the closure, seam, texture or applicator — product only partly in frame. Shoot on a 35mm reportage at f/4, framing for deep negative space above the subject with a low horizon.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with hard side light with 80 percent of the frame falling into shadow. Stage the product on or against book-matched marble, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a pastel low-contrast grade with a lifted black point. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
